fraud_scenarios.name: Cash skimming attempt (delete cash order to hide sale)
fraud_scenarios.vector: Cashier sells 100€ cash order → pockets money → tries to delete/cancel order to hide the sale

defenses_verified.behavior: PAID orders cannot be destroyed without `pos-destroy-paid` Spatie permission — abort 403
If order has fiscal_sequence_no AND falls inside a CLOSED Z window (opened_at < created_at <= closed_at), destroy aborts 409 'sealed by Z report'

Even soft-delete (the only path admitted) writes audit_logs row `order.destroyed` with full forensic payload + ActionLog row. composition_snapshot survives on order_items because RestrictOnDelete + DELETE triggers
Transitioning OUT of CANCELED/REJECTED/RETURNED requires Admin role — a cashier cannot un-cancel and silently re-mark as PAID later
PREPARING/ACCEPT → CANCELED is permitted but requires reason (assertAllows + requiresReason). Audit row in order_status_transitions.
Even if cashier UPDATEs/DELETEs the row directly, BEFORE UPDATE / BEFORE DELETE trigger SIGNAL 45000 (MySQL) + RAISE ABORT (SQLite); model also throws RuntimeException

fraud_scenarios.residual_risk: If a cashier with `pos-destroy-paid` permission destroys a cash order BEFORE the Z is closed, the order soft-deletes but the audit_logs row + ActionLog row preserve forensic trail. cash_movements remain immutable (cash_movements_no_delete trigger). Sale visible to owner via audit_logs.action='order.destroyed' query. NOT silent.

fraud_scenarios.name: Fake refund pocket money (counter-entry abuse)
fraud_scenarios.vector: Cashier creates fake refund for 50€ → pockets cash from drawer → drawer reconciliation should expose -50€ écart

defenses_verified.behavior: Counter-entry only allowed if parent.fiscal_sequence_no != null → cannot refund unfinalized orders
SealedOrderGuard::assertSealed enforces parent is in a CLOSED Z window — refund-with-counter-entry path strictly post-Z. Pre-Z refunds use standard OrderService pre-Z RETURNED path.
If parent.status == RETURNED already, throws 422 'duplicate mirror' — defense-in-depth above UNIQUE(parent_order_id) index added by migration 2026_05_19_200000 (heal A.3)
reason is required (trim non-empty) → cashier MUST justify the refund. Stored in mirror.reason + audit_logs payload.

userId resolved from Auth::id() — audit_logs.user_id captures the cashier identity (H2-HEAL-02 cashier attribution). Audit action 'order.refund.counter_entry' with payload {parent_order_id, parent_serial_no, parent_fiscal_sequence_no, mirror_fiscal_sequence_no, mirror_total, mirror_payments_count, reason}. Forensic chain unbreakable.

Mirrors ALL parent OrderPayments with NEGATED amounts AND tendered/change_amount → drawer reconciliation aggregates show expected = original_in - mirror_out, so the -50€ refund hits expected. Owner inspecting variance sees -50€ écart vs 0€ deposit on the drawer → IMMEDIATE RED FLAG.

If |variance| > config('cash.variance_threshold_eur') (default 2.00€), reconcileSession throws CashVarianceRequiresApprovalException unless variance_reason provided AND user holds cash.reconcile.variance.override permission (Admin / Branch Manager).

fraud_scenarios.residual_risk: The +50€ pocketed cash WILL surface as a -50€ écart in the drawer reconciliation (expected = opening + Σmovements_signed; mirror payment is a CASH OUT movement). If owner reviews variance reports, fraud is caught. Owner reliance: variance threshold + monthly Z review.
fraud_scenarios.verdict: GREEN — fraud is detectable & forensically attributed

fraud_scenarios.name: Z-report manipulation (early close to misdate sales)
fraud_scenarios.vector: Cashier closes Z at 14h instead of 23h → sales between 14h-23h fall in next day's Z (misdated)

defenses_verified.behavior: Acquires Cache::lock('z_report_b{n}') 10s TTL; validates the entire historical chain via verifyChain() AND extended chain via FiscalChainValidator::assertChainIntegrity() BEFORE reserving sequence. Concurrent simultaneous opens → one wins, others throw 'cannot acquire lock'.
Same cache lock + DB transaction + lockForUpdate on the open Z. Re-verifies chain before signing. NO DAYLIGHT BOUNDARY CHECK — Z can be closed at any time of day.
Half-open window (opened_at, closed_at]. Sales AFTER closed_at fall to next Z window. Sealed orders are NF525-immutable (cannot move between Zs).
z_report.close action audited with z_report_id + sequence_no + closed_by + signature_prefix → forensic trail for early closes
Sealing service signs (branch_id, prev_hash, sequence_no, aggregates, closed_at). closed_at is in UTC ISO-8601 (POS-9-H.2.7 / F-B4) → owner reviewing signature timestamps sees the early close.

fraud_scenarios.residual_risk: The early Z close attack moves sales between actual-close and end-of-day to the NEXT Z. Sales are NOT hidden (chain integrity preserved, all sales sequenced + signed). However, day-level fiscal accounting is shifted. Owner must verify Z close timestamps match expected business-day boundary (end-of-day report habit).

open_concerns.severity: P2 (V1.0.2 BACKLOG — operational discipline, not technical vulnerability)
open_concerns.concern: ZReportService.close() has NO same-day boundary check. A cashier closing at 14h00 instead of 23h00 will not be technically blocked. Defense relies on owner habit of reviewing daily Z closes.
open_concerns.recommendation: V1.0.2: add config('fiscal.z_close_business_day_end_hour', 23) guard — refuse close before that hour unless permission `fiscal.z_close.before_eod_override` (Admin only). Reuses CashDrawerService manager-gate pattern. ETA ~2h dev + ~1h test.

fraud_scenarios.verdict: AMBER — sales not hidden but operational discipline required for boundary correctness

fraud_scenarios.name: audit_logs cover tracks (UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE/ALTER)
fraud_scenarios.vector: Cashier-admin tries to UPDATE/DELETE specific audit_logs rows to remove evidence

defenses_verified.behavior: static::updating() + static::deleting() both throw RuntimeException unconditionally → cannot delete or update via Eloquent
MySQL/MariaDB triggers audit_logs_no_update + audit_logs_no_delete raise SIGNAL SQLSTATE '45000'; SQLite triggers use RAISE(ABORT, ...). Even DBAs with raw SQL access cannot bypass.

MySQL TRUNCATE bypasses BEFORE DELETE triggers BUT is mitigated via `scripts/deploy/server-setup.sh:355-376` — applies `REVOKE DROP, ALTER ON audit_logs FROM '${APP_DB_USER}'@'localhost'` (Ansible CVP0-1 equivalent). Verified: server-setup.sh executes REVOKE DROP/ALTER on both audit_logs + z_reports POST-MIGRATE (idempotent, log warning if table not yet created).
If APP_ENV=production, down() throws RuntimeException 'Refusing to drop audit_logs ... NF525 mandates 6-year retention' → migrate:rollback cannot wipe audit_logs in production

fraud_scenarios.residual_risk: TRUNCATE permission is NOT explicitly revoked by server-setup.sh (script revokes DROP+ALTER but not TRUNCATE). However, TRUNCATE on MySQL requires the DROP privilege on InnoDB tables (because TRUNCATE re-CREATEs the table), so DROP REVOKE blocks TRUNCATE indirectly. Confirmation needed via production smoke test. Additionally, ALTER REVOKE prevents disabling the trigger.

open_concerns.concern: server-setup.sh REVOKEs DROP+ALTER but does not explicitly include TRUNCATE in the privilege list. On MySQL 8, TRUNCATE requires DROP — implicit block. But explicit `REVOKE DROP, ALTER, TRUNCATE` would make the intent unmistakable (defense-in-depth).
open_concerns.recommendation: V1.0.2: add explicit TRUNCATE to REVOKE statement in scripts/deploy/server-setup.sh:370 — pure additive harden.

fraud_scenarios.verdict: GREEN — 4-layer defense (model + DB trigger + REVOKE DROP/ALTER + production migration guard)

fraud_scenarios.name: composition_snapshot manipulation (charge less but record more)
fraud_scenarios.vector: Create order with cheap items → after order, UPDATE composition_snapshot to expensive items to bilk fiscal

defenses_verified.behavior: Verified: 5 write sites all in OrderItem::create()/insert payload arrays at order creation (OrderService.php:484, 916, 1417 + FrontendOrderService.php:442 + PricingService.php:291 + RefundWithCounterEntryService.php:146 — last is mirror copy). ZERO ->composition_snapshot = ... write sites. ZERO OrderItem::where()->update() callsites in app/. ZERO update() with composition_snapshot key in payload (verified by Read of OrderService:480-490, :910-920, :1410-1420 + FrontendOrderService:438-446 + PricingService:285-295).
composition_snapshot IS fillable on OrderItem (line 44) — mass-assignable in CREATE. NO updating() guard at model layer. NO DB UPDATE trigger on order_items.

PricingService::calculateOrder is the SSOT for price calculation. Frontend cannot push arbitrary composition_snapshot — backend builds it from item_id + variations + extras via CompositionSnapshotBuilder. Validates ownership of variations/extras against the parent item.

fraud_scenarios.residual_risk: NO CODE PATH currently updates composition_snapshot post-creation, but the column lacks a DB-level UPDATE trigger and the model lacks an updating() guard. An attacker with raw SQL access to MySQL can `UPDATE order_items SET composition_snapshot = '...' WHERE id=X`. Mitigation = same REVOKE strategy as audit_logs: REVOKE UPDATE on order_items would break legitimate workflows (refunds copy composition_snapshot but use INSERT, not UPDATE — so REVOKE UPDATE on order_items would actually be ENFORCEABLE).

open_concerns.concern: composition_snapshot has no DB-level immutability guard analogous to audit_logs. If a malicious DBA / leaked DB creds attacker UPDATEs the column directly, the fiscal receipt content (item names, prices, sauces, variations) can be altered AFTER the order seal. The HMAC chain in audit_logs/z_reports does NOT cover composition_snapshot — only Z aggregates.
open_concerns.recommendation: V1.0.2 owner-gate: (1) add BEFORE UPDATE trigger on order_items that raises SIGNAL 45000 if NEW.composition_snapshot != OLD.composition_snapshot (column-level immutability — allows other field updates like instruction); OR (2) extend audit_logs HMAC payload to include order_items.composition_snapshot hash on order seal — tamper-evident. Option 1 is simpler / faster (~1d dev + 2h test). Already documented in BRAIN §2 as 'composition_snapshot immutability 100% preserved' but the attestation is callsite-based, not DB-trigger-based.

fraud_scenarios.verdict: AMBER — currently safe by absence of callsite but lacks defense-in-depth

fraud_scenarios.name: fiscal_sequence_no gap (skip number to hide sale)
fraud_scenarios.vector: Try to create order with fiscal_sequence_no skipping number; or try to UPDATE existing order's fiscal_sequence_no to reuse a deleted slot

defenses_verified.behavior: next() returns MAX(fiscal_sequence_no)+1 per branch atomically: Cache::lock('fiscal_seq_b{n}') 5s TTL + DB::transaction + Order::query()->lockForUpdate()->max('fiscal_sequence_no'). No callsite passes client-side sequence_no.
withoutGlobalScope(BranchScope) + withTrashed() ensures MAX considers soft-deleted orders → cannot reuse a sequence_no by soft-deleting the holder
Per FiscalSequenceService docstring line 22: unique key prevents two parallel allocs from colliding even if cache lock fails. lockForUpdate is the storage-tier defense in depth.

defenses_verified.layer: Order model — verified no fillable callsite passes fiscal_sequence_no from request
defenses_verified.behavior: OrderService :484 / :916 / :1417 build order rows server-side; fiscal_sequence_no allocated via FiscalSequenceService::next($branchId). RefundWithCounterEntryService::100 also allocates fresh sequence_no.

fraud_scenarios.residual_risk: An attacker with raw SQL UPDATE on orders could try `UPDATE orders SET fiscal_sequence_no=999 WHERE id=X` → violates UNIQUE constraint if value exists, or leaves a gap if value is fresh. Mitigated by REVOKE UPDATE on orders.fiscal_sequence_no (column-level GRANT) at deploy. Currently server-setup.sh REVOKEs only DROP/ALTER on the table — not column-level UPDATE.

open_concerns.severity: P2 (V1.0.X cloud-prep — single-resto local DB scope acceptable for V1)
open_concerns.concern: No column-level REVOKE on orders.fiscal_sequence_no — a malicious DBA can in theory rewrite a sequence number. Single-tenant local Le Cayenne deploys with non-shared DB creds: acceptable. Multi-tenant cloud V2: must add column-level REVOKE or BEFORE UPDATE trigger gating fiscal_sequence_no rewrites.
open_concerns.recommendation: V1.0.X cloud-prep: trigger `IF NEW.fiscal_sequence_no IS NOT NULL AND OLD.fiscal_sequence_no IS NOT NULL AND NEW.fiscal_sequence_no != OLD.fiscal_sequence_no THEN SIGNAL 45000; END IF` on orders table.

fraud_scenarios.verdict: GREEN — V1 single-resto safe; V2 cloud needs column-level harden

fraud_scenarios.name: Drawer count manipulation (input wrong count to hide écart)
fraud_scenarios.vector: End-of-shift drawer reconciliation: cashier inputs wrong closing_amount to hide écart

defenses_verified.behavior: expected = round(opening_amount + Σ(movements signedAmount), 2). variance = round(closing_amount - expected, 2). Both fields persisted on cash_drawer_sessions row. Variance is COMPUTED, not user-supplied — cashier inputs closing_amount but variance is calculated by the system.

If |variance| > config('cash.variance_threshold_eur', 2.00€), throws CashVarianceRequiresApprovalException UNLESS (1) variance_reason provided (string, non-empty, max 255) AND (2) actor holds `cash.reconcile.variance.override` permission (Admin + Branch Manager). Reason is mandatory in payload.

Reconcile audit_logs row contains expected + variance + variance_reason + threshold + over_threshold. NF525 evidence. Cashier cannot edit retrospectively (audit immutable + reconciled status terminal).
Cannot reconcile a RECONCILED session (terminal). Idempotent on second call. Owner reviewing audit_logs for action='cash.session.reconciled' filters over_threshold=true for variance reports.

defenses_verified.layer: CashDrawerService.php:132-160 (Sprint H2 F-11 manager-gate routine close)
defenses_verified.behavior: If config('cash.manager_gate_routine_close', false) is true, ANY close (variance OR no-variance) requires `cash.reconcile.variance.override` permission. Opt-in for multi-cashier deploys.

fraud_scenarios.residual_risk: If cashier inputs closing_amount that matches expected (e.g. 100€ expected, 100€ input but only 50€ physically in drawer), no variance is detected — fraud requires the cashier to also alter the physical drawer count which is the human-supervised step. Owner mitigation: physical spot-checks + dual-witness counts (managerial discipline, not code).
fraud_scenarios.verdict: GREEN — system catches discrepancy; physical drawer count is owner-supervised

fraud_scenarios.name: Fake DUPLICATA reprint (alter receipt content)
fraud_scenarios.vector: Cashier reprints customer receipt → tries to alter receipt content during reprint (fake amount)

defenses_verified.behavior: Atomic UPDATE orders SET receipt_print_count = COALESCE(...,0)+1 scoped to branch_id → no count-loss under concurrent prints, no cross-branch leak
is_duplicata = newCount >= 2 → automatically marks DUPLICATA when count >= 2 (W9.B G3). UI ReceiptDuplicataMarker.vue renders the legal mention.

Audit action `pos.receipt.print` (first) or `pos.receipt.reprint` (duplicata) written via AuditLogService. Payload {order_id, print_count_after, print_count_before, is_duplicata}. Best-effort: audit_emitted=false in response if chain failure, surfaced to UI for manager warning.

Receipt content rendered from Order + OrderItem.composition_snapshot — FROZEN at order creation. Cashier cannot alter amount during reprint (would need to also alter composition_snapshot which has no callsite to UPDATE).

fraud_scenarios.residual_risk: Receipt is rendered from frozen DB state; reprint cannot change displayed amount unless attacker first compromises composition_snapshot (see F5) — same defense.
fraud_scenarios.verdict: GREEN — DUPLICATA marker forensic + content frozen

fraud_scenarios.name: Reverse-engineer HMAC secret (read .env to forge audit logs)
fraud_scenarios.vector: Insider with shell access reads .env to extract FISCAL_AUDIT_SECRET → forge audit_logs rows

defenses_verified.behavior: Verified 8 fail-fast checks at boot: POS_SIMULATION_HARDWARE, PAYMENT_BYPASS, PRINTING_BYPASS, APP_DEBUG, IDEMPOTENCY_MIDDLEWARE_ENABLED, LOYALTY_QR_SECRET, APP_URL, BROADCAST_DRIVER, QUEUE_CONNECTION, CACHE_DRIVER (forbidden array/null). FISCAL_AUDIT_SECRET itself enforced via dev_sentinels check + min_secret_length=32 in AuditLogService::assertProductionSafe() and ZReportService::assertProductionSafe().
Production refuses secrets in dev_sentinels list OR shorter than 32 chars → cannot deploy with weak secret. RuntimeException at first write attempt.
BRAIN §2 attests 706 LOC server-setup includes .env permission discipline (file owner web user, 600 perms). Not directly verified in this audit (deploy script scope).

fraud_scenarios.residual_risk: If insider has shell access AND can read .env (600 perms not respected, sudo abuse, log file leak), they can compute HMAC chain rows. HOWEVER: even forged rows must respect (branch_id, prev_hash) UNIQUE index — a forged row collides with subsequent legitimate rows. Detection: AuditLogService::verifyChain() re-walks the chain and returns the first tampered row id. Owner runs periodic verifyChain() and detects mismatches. Single-tenant Le Cayenne local: physical access control is the primary defense (server in locked back-office).

open_concerns.concern: Multi-instance cloud cutover (V2 SaaS) increases shell-access surface. Secret rotation cron + HSM/Vault integration recommended. Currently FISCAL_AUDIT_SECRET is plain .env value.
open_concerns.recommendation: V1.0.X cloud-prep: integrate with AWS Secrets Manager / Hetzner Vault. Rotate quarterly via documented procedure (docs/FISCAL_SECRETS.md exists per migration ref).

fraud_scenarios.verdict: GREEN — V1 LOCAL safe (physical access control); cloud V2 needs vault integration

fraud_scenarios.name: Loyalty redeem fraud (redeem + refund pocket points + cash)
fraud_scenarios.vector: Cashier redeems 50€ loyalty discount on order → refunds order → pockets cash AND keeps points (or vice versa)

defenses_verified.behavior: Mirror order creation invokes app(LoyaltyService::class)->refundPoints($parent, 'pos') unconditionally. refundPoints is no-op-safe if loyalty_customer_code is null. Inside the same DB::transaction → atomic with mirror order + mirror payments + audit row.

Idempotent NOOP via early-detect: queries existing LoyaltyTransaction WHERE order_id AND type='manual_add' BEFORE any mutation. Duplicate refund attempt returns silently (no double-credit). Owner Q1 decision: NOOP not 409 throw (planner-recommended).

Atomic increment loyalty_points + LoyaltyTransaction::create('manual_add'). UNIQUE index (user_id, order_id, type) at migration 2026_03_26_075919 prevents duplicate ledger entries even if early-detect race lost.
lockForUpdate on User row (non-sqlite) → concurrent refund attempts on same loyalty customer serialize.
LOYALTY_QR_SECRET enforced in production boot guard. Loyalty QR scans cryptographically signed → replay attack blocked. Cross-surface fraud heal complete per BRAIN.

fraud_scenarios.residual_risk: If H2-HEAL-04 TTC-tax-double-count fix is in place (BRAIN attests fixed), legitimate refund flow returns the original points value. Cashier cannot pocket both cash AND points — points return on refund. Refund pocket cash requires cashier to also tamper drawer count (F7 caught by variance gate).
fraud_scenarios.verdict: GREEN — full atomic reversal + signed QR + idempotent NOOP

fraud_scenarios.name: Tax category manipulation (change item tax_rate to 0% for fiscal underreporting)
fraud_scenarios.vector: Cashier-admin changes item's tax_rate to 0% mid-day → new orders apply 0% TVA → fiscal underreporting in next Z

defenses_verified.behavior: ItemController::update gated by permission:items_edit (defense-in-depth per ItemRequest.php:23-30 authorize()). ItemRequest.php:49 validates tax_id as ['nullable','numeric','not_in:0']. Cashier without items_edit permission cannot change tax.

Items reference taxes via tax_id FK (not raw tax_rate). Changing tax requires creating/selecting an existing Tax row. The TAX ENTITY itself is also gated (likely by similar items_edit or settings permission).

defenses_verified.layer: composition_snapshot freezes tax at order creation
defenses_verified.behavior: When order created, OrderItem.tax_rate + tax_amount + tax_name are written from the item's tax AT THE TIME of creation. composition_snapshot includes tax breakdown. Changing item's tax tomorrow does NOT retroactively affect yesterday's orders → Z aggregates remain consistent.
ItemService logs item updates (verified pattern from BRAIN). Tax change creates an action_logs / audit_logs trail attributable to actor.

open_concerns.concern: No mandatory 'Z-close before tax_rate change' guard. Tax changes mid-day yield mid-day rate splits in Z aggregates (correctly broken down per tax_rate in total_by_tax_rate column).
open_concerns.recommendation: Optional V1.0.X: log warning on Tax update if there's an OPEN Z. Not blocking — owner discipline + audit trail is sufficient.

fraud_vectors_found.title: composition_snapshot lacks DB-level UPDATE guard
fraud_vectors_found.scenario: An attacker with raw SQL access to MySQL can `UPDATE order_items SET composition_snapshot = '<altered>' WHERE id=X` AFTER the order is sealed. The HMAC chain in audit_logs/z_reports does NOT cover the per-item composition snapshot — only Z aggregates. This means a malicious DBA / leaked DB creds attacker can alter fiscal receipt content (item names, prices, sauces, variations) post-seal undetected.
fraud_vectors_found.where: app/Models/OrderItem.php:31-56 (fillable includes composition_snapshot, no static::updating() guard). No BEFORE UPDATE trigger on order_items table in any migration.
fraud_vectors_found.currently_unreachable_via: Verified zero callsites that UPDATE composition_snapshot in app/. Defense is callsite-absence, not enforcement.
fraud_vectors_found.exploitability_v1: Local single-tenant Le Cayenne: requires physical access + DB creds. LOW for V1 production. HIGH for V2 SaaS cloud cutover.
fraud_vectors_found.recommendation: V1.0.2 owner-gate (preferred Option 1): add migration creating BEFORE UPDATE trigger on order_items: `IF NEW.composition_snapshot IS NOT NULL AND OLD.composition_snapshot IS NOT NULL AND NEW.composition_snapshot != OLD.composition_snapshot THEN SIGNAL SQLSTATE '45000' SET MESSAGE_TEXT = 'order_items.composition_snapshot is immutable post-seal (NF525)'; END IF;` Allows other field updates (instruction, etc.) which are non-fiscal. ETA ~1d dev + ~2h SQLite parity + ~3h test. Option 2 (HMAC chain extension): more invasive, defer to V2.

fraud_vectors_found.title: ZReportService.close() has no business-day-end boundary check
fraud_vectors_found.scenario: A cashier closing Z at 14h00 instead of EOD 23h00 will not be technically blocked. Sales between 14h-23h fall to NEXT Z (misdated). Owner reviewing daily Z reports notices the off-hour close timestamp — but defense is currently 100% manual review.
fraud_vectors_found.where: app/Services/Fiscal/ZReportService.php:180-286 (close method has NO closed_at >= EOD guard)
fraud_vectors_found.exploitability: Sales NOT hidden — chain integrity preserved, all sales sequenced + signed. But day-level fiscal accounting is shifted across the date boundary.
fraud_vectors_found.recommendation: V1.0.2: add config('fiscal.z_close_business_day_end_hour', 23) optional guard — refuse close before that hour unless permission `fiscal.z_close.before_eod_override` (Admin only). Reuses CashDrawerService manager-gate pattern. ETA ~2h dev + ~1h test.

fraud_vectors_found.title: server-setup.sh REVOKE statement lacks explicit TRUNCATE in privilege list
fraud_vectors_found.scenario: scripts/deploy/server-setup.sh:370 issues `REVOKE DROP, ALTER` but not TRUNCATE. On MySQL 8, TRUNCATE on InnoDB requires the DROP privilege (because TRUNCATE re-CREATEs the table internally), so DROP REVOKE blocks TRUNCATE indirectly. However, explicit inclusion in the privilege list eliminates ambiguity for future MySQL version semantics or storage engine changes.
fraud_vectors_found.exploitability: Currently NONE — DROP REVOKE implies TRUNCATE REVOKE on InnoDB. Future-proofing concern only.
fraud_vectors_found.recommendation: V1.0.2: add explicit TRUNCATE to REVOKE statement → `REVOKE DROP, ALTER, TRUNCATE ON ...`. Pure additive harden. ETA ~5min edit + redeploy.

fraud_vectors_found.scenario: An attacker with raw SQL UPDATE on orders could attempt `UPDATE orders SET fiscal_sequence_no=X WHERE id=Y`. The attacker would still need to manage the chain — Z aggregates use MAX, so a gap is detectable on next allocation.

fraud_vectors_found.exploitability: Single-tenant local Le Cayenne with non-shared DB creds: LOW. Multi-tenant cloud V2: ELEVATED.
fraud_vectors_found.recommendation: V1.0.X cloud-prep: BEFORE UPDATE trigger gating fiscal_sequence_no rewrites. Defer to V2.
